ai.description: *Hemidactylus vijayraghavani* is a small gecko reaching 45 mm SVL. It is pale brown with dark dorsal crossbands and possesses 8–10 subdigital lamellae on the fourth toe and smooth ventral scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus vijayraghavani* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of 8–10 enlarged, strongly keeled, and mucronate tubercles arranged in regular longitudinal rows on its dorsum.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus vijayraghavani* inhabits rocky outcrops and boulder-strewn landscapes within dry deciduous forests and scrublands of the Indian peninsula.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus vijayraghavani* is a nocturnal gecko that actively hunts small insects on rock surfaces and exhibits rapid flight behavior when threatened by predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus vijayraghavani* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled, spherical eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus vijayraghavani* is endemic to the rocky outcrops of the Deccan Plateau in the Indian states of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
